payload.claim: `reconcile` treats "currently in an in-flight state" as synonymous with "corpse" and stamps every such row `ORPHANED` unconditionally (lines 122-124), with no check on `updated_at` age, elapsed time, or any liveness signal for the cell that might still be actively running that task. This holds in every test fixture, because the fixtures seed rows directly with `set_task_state`/`set_task_package` and no cell is ever actually running concurrently. In production it does not hold: `saffron queue` now calls `reconcile` before every scan (`cli.py` ~line 274), and `saffron queue`'s own docstring still advertises it as a side-effect-free preview ("without starting a cell or writing anything to the ledger"), so an operator running `saffron queue` (or `saffron reconcile`) while any task for that repo is genuinely mid-phase (IMPLEMENTING, GATING, REVIEWING, etc.) will have that live task's row silently relabelled `ORPHANED`. Because `ORPHANED` is in `scheduler.REQUEUE_STATES`, the very next `build_queue` scan will then hand the same `task_id`/branch back out as resumable, i.e. as a fresh candidate to run again, while the original cell is still writing to that same task's rows and branch — a real double-execution and lost-update path, not a hypothetical one, since `scheduler.py`'s own `Candidate` docstring explicitly flagged this exact liveness question as the thing the ORPHANED-stamping write would need to get right ("a corpse this spec does not stamp `ORPHANED`") and this diff answers it by stamping every in-flight row regardless of whether it is actually a corpse.
